scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I need to figure out if the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person in question is a 21-year-old woman who gifted her two cousins, Tj (15) and Ked (13), each an iPhone when the new models were released. Ked had been stealing money from extended family members and admitted to it. There was a fight, and Ked's parents defended him, not caring about the stealing and cutting off the extended family. Later, Ked apologized and made amends, but his parents remained stubborn and refused to admit they were wrong, hating the extended family now.

During a housewarming party, both cousins wanted to attend. Ked's parents told him he couldn't go, fearing the extended family would accuse him again. Tj's parents told him he could decide for himself and trusted him. Tj went to the party, but his phone blew up with messages from his parents yelling at him, calling him a disappointment, and saying if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. Tj asked to be left out of the drama, but they insisted. When he came back, they grounded him and took his phone away for two weeks. Meanwhile, Ked, who admitted to stealing, never got punished.

The person is disgusted by how the parents are raising their kids and lost respect for them. She told them she couldn't control their discipline but that the phone wasn't their property to take away. She said she wouldn't let Tj use the phone behind their backs but since it was her gift, she wanted to hold onto it until the two weeks were up. The parents made a big deal, and other extended family members told her to stay out of it, saying she's only asking for the phone because she thinks they're treating him unfairly. It's agreed that the parents are horrible. If they were fair, she wouldn't have asked for the phone back. She thinks they're trying to establish dominance and control Tj with cruel punishment, so she took some power away by asking for her gift back.

Now, I need to evaluate whether her action is morally acceptable. Let's break it down.

First, she gifted the phone to Tj. Legally, once the gift is given, it's his property. However, since he's a minor, his parents might have control over it. But she's arguing that it's her gift, so she should have the right to take it back if she feels the punishment is unfair.

She's intervening because she believes the parents are treating Tj unfairly, using the phone as a cruel punishment. She's trying to protect him from their control by taking the phone back. On the other hand, some might argue that she's overstepping by taking the phone, as it's the parents' right to discipline their child, even if she disagrees with their methods.

But considering the context, the parents have a history of poor judgment, not punishing Ked for stealing, and treating Tj harshly. They're using the phone as a tool to control him, which seems excessive. She's trying to prevent further harm by taking the phone, which could be seen as a form of support for Tj.

However, by taking the phone, she's also interfering in the parents' authority, which could lead to more conflict. But given the parents' behavior, it's understandable she feels the need to step in.

So, is her action morally acceptable? I think yes, because she's trying to protect Tj from unfair treatment and control. She's not keeping the phone for herself but is holding onto it to prevent the parents from using it as a tool of punishment. She's also respecting the parents' right to discipline but drawing a line when she feels it's excessive.

Therefore, the action is morally acceptable.
